editorial_policy: Classification, citations and form evidence are separate. A source URL is a research pointer, not a guarantee that each claim is verified. Grammar-derived forms are not independently text-attested. No scholar has peer-reviewed this data.

words.notes: Source: Lockhart, Nahuatl as Written p. 212; Karttunen p. 22 (quoted in the linked entry).

words.translation: My song rises up toward the sky.

words.notes: Additional direct plural witness: https://gdn.iib.unam.mx/diccionario/xochitl/76692
Animacy is flagged CONTEXTUAL, not simply “animate”: this is a noun-class exception associated with personification.
Orthographic variant citlalli is recorded in the same source; do not merge its form with all senses indiscriminately.

words.meaning: earth; soil; land; plot of land
words.notes: The plural is a period-marked historical exception, NOT the basic productive classical paradigm.

words.meaning: stone; hard object; counting classifier in certain uses

words.notes: The linked entry cites Chimalpahin, Codex Chimalpahin vol. 2 pp. 140–141 and Annals of His Time pp. 178–179.
Source page specifically cautions that altepeme/altepemeh is very scarce in colonial alphabetic texts.

words.meaning: person; human being; sometimes noble person
noble person; child in possessed and honorific contexts
words.notes: Different from the suffix -pil “child.”
Secondary witness: https://gdn.iib.unam.mx/diccionario/coyome
Florentine Codex Book 11 records toto(tl)/totome as singular/plural in the linked lexical record.

words.meaning: commoner; subject; later an Indigenous person
words.notes: Direct plural headword: https://nahuatl.wired-humanities.org/content/macehualtin

words.meaning: snake; serpent; twin in a distinct extended sense

words.notes: Exact historical plural: https://gdn.iib.unam.mx/diccionario/ocelome/154981

words.meaning: to speak; make a pronouncement; speak authoritatively
words.notes: Ortographic variants tlahtoa, tlatoa, tlahtohua.

words.meaning: to cry, weep; make animal cries
to live; reside; go about doing
to live; come to life; hatch
to count/read (without specifying object); also pray
and; but; well; introduces another statement
day; solar warmth; day sign; solar life force
words.notes: Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 149r col. 2; Karttunen 1992, p. 246. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Molina and Karttunen distinguish physical solar warmth, day, and culturally specific vital force.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 40v; Karttunen 1992, pp. 342–343. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Usually possessed; see -yōllō. Do not infer that the 16th c. land-measure yollotli is identical to the physical heart lemma.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 32v col. 1; Karttunen 1992, p. 93. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Plural reduplicates -pōch-; not simply addition of a productive suffix.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 140v col. 1; Karttunen 1992, p. 266. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Suppletive base in some inflected forms; do not generate *tlatoanimeh as a default.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 93r col. 2; Lockhart 2001, p. 233. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Also a locative/relational expression. ENL confirms organizational sense, not just building.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 93r col. 2; Karttunen 1992, p. 217. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Compare tecpan; ENL Doc. 26 line 27 records institutional rather than necessarily architectural reference.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 55v col. 1; Karttunen 1992, p. 144. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Homographic metztli meaning thigh/leg must be kept as a distinct lexical sense; do not conflate vowel length.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 100r col. 2; Karttunen 1992, p. 227. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Church/temple usage varies by colonial period; this is a full building noun.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Lockhart 2001, p. 237; Launey 2011, p. 64. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Also appears in numeral/quantifier constructions; not a transparent regular plural paradigm.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 137r col. 2; Karttunen 1992, p. 263. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Patientive nominal derived from a verb; a mass/abstract use may lack overt plural.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 24v col. 1; Karttunen 1992, p. 41. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Reduplicated plural explicitly recorded, not mechanically -meh.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 80r col. 1; Karttunen 1992, p. 188. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Abstract noun, not classified as a finite verb.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 105v col. 1; Karttunen 1992, p. 233. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Source describes duty/office/tribute as well as physical work.

words.meaning: year; comet; grass or turquoise in other senses
words.notes: Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 159v col. 2. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Polysemous/homographic. Separate calendrical year from other possible lexical senses; grammatical animacy not established for all.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Karttunen 1992, p. 46; Lockhart 2001, p. 214. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Usually occurs possessed or as a locative; do not infer a regular bare plural just from -meh suffix notation.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 12r col. 1; Karttunen 1992, p. 24. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Often possessed; alternate bound shapes -can and -camac need separate documentation.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 48v col. 1; Karttunen 1992, p. 121. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. The combining element -īx is not a free nominative headword.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 51v col. 1; Karttunen 1992, pp. 133–134. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Arms/hands and measurement senses; alternating bound stem -mā; do not collapse into the separate land-measure matl.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 34r col. 2; Karttunen 1992, p. 95. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Inalienable body-part vocabulary may show possessed stems, not a straightforward plural.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 68r col. 1; Karttunen 1992, p. 168. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Karttunen lists plural suffix -tin; no independently checked full surface spelling in this batch.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 21r col. 1; Karttunen 1992, p. 52. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Shield noun, sometimes paired with arrow to refer metaphorically to war.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 96v col. 1; Karttunen 1992, p. 221. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Plural with reduplication of -pōch- recorded by Karttunen.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 126r col. 1; Karttunen 1992, p. 281. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Agent noun formed with -ni, not the finite verb mati.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 101r; Karttunen 1992, p. 227. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. An agent noun; ritual/Christian reference may change with genre and period.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 160v col. 2; Karttunen 1992, p. 329. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Can be generic fruit or specific sour fruit; keep senses separate in contextual analysis.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 72v col. 1; Karttunen 1992, p. 172. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Not automatically equivalent to the prickly pear cactus plant itself.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 151v col. 1; Karttunen 1992, p. 311. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Karttunen lists -meh plural marking; exact full plural spelling not independently verified here.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 29r col. 2; Karttunen 1992, p. 78. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Ye-tl is an attested dialectal initial-glide variant; do not manufacture plural forms.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 21r col. 1; Karttunen 1992, p. 52. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Historical form appears in ENL Don Juan document; not all uses denote a single pepper.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 56v col. 1; Karttunen 1992, p. 147. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. ENL Coyoacan document locates four worked fields, using this lexical item.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 75v col. 2; Karttunen 1992, p. 176. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Second-vowel length varies in sources; retained source spelling for headword.

words.meaning: wind; breeze; divine Wind in distinct sense
words.notes: Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 28r col. 2; Lockhart 2001, p. 217. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Ordinary meteorological wind inanimate, personified deity in a separate sense; do not impose a single animacy rule.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Karttunen 1992, p. 108; Carochi fol. 85v. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Animal noun; day-name use is proper-name context.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 104v col. 2; Karttunen 1992, p. 218. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Karttunen supplies plural suffix -meh; exact full spelling not independently checked.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 62v col. 2; Karttunen 1992, p. 158. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Reduplicated plural recorded explicitly by Karttunen.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 13r; Karttunen 1992, p. 21. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Temporal noun, not a finite verb.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Karttunen 1992, p. 132. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Lexical record cites Karttunen; no Molina citation was located in this specific entry.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 66v col. 2; Karttunen 1992, p. 164. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Abstract noun derived from truth/being true.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 148r; Karttunen 1992, p. 242. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Do not confuse the name noun with tocatl spider; attached possessive i-toca is not an absolutive.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 41v col. 1; Karttunen 1992, p. 340. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Can occur in adverbial nighttime constructions.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 37v col. 1; Karttunen 1992, p. 104. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Not identical in meaning to tonalli, which also covers solar heat/ritual day-sign.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Karttunen 1992, p. 166; Lockhart 2001, p. 226. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. A nominalization of nemi; not a finite verb.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 142r col. 2; Karttunen 1992, p. 300. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Can be plural in English translation without implying a Nahuatl plural morpheme.

Lexical meaning and lemma checked against Online Nahuatl Dictionary; Molina 1571 II, fol. 82r col. 1; Karttunen 1992, p. 196. Not all morphological fields have been separately attested. Morphologically related to pilli but recorded as a distinct headword; do not conflate senses.
